Nutella bombolini ✨ Ingredients  Donuts - 435g bread flour (3 cups + 2 tbsp) - 68g granulated sugar (1/3 cup) - 185g whole milk (3/4 cup) - 60g unsalted butter, softened (4 tbsp) - 7g active dry yeast (2 1/4 tsp) - 2 large eggs - 1 tsp vanilla extract  - 1/2 tsp salt - Canola oil for frying Filling/topping - 7.7 oz Nutella  - Granulated sugar (to cover donuts) Instructions  - In a bowl, combine warm milk and 1 tbsp sugar. Sprinkle yeast over the top, stir lightly, and let sit 5–10 minutes until foamy. - Add eggs, 1/3 cup sugar, vanilla extract and mix again until well combined. - Add flour to mixture. Mix until a rough dough forms. - Begin kneading. Once the dough starts to come together, gradually add the softened butter (1 tbsp at a time), kneading until fully incorporated before adding more. - Continue kneading 8–10 minutes by hand or 5–6 minutes in a stand mixer, until smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky. - Transfer dough to a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1–1½ hours, or until doubled in size. - Punch down dough and separate into 12 balls (weighing 65g each) - Place onto parchment lined tray cover loosely and let rise 30–40 minutes, until puffy. - In a large skillet heat oil to 325–335°F (aim for 330°F) - Fry 2–3 minutes per side - Flip every 30–45 seconds for even color - Fry until golden brown - Remove donuts from oil place onto a wire rack  - Toss in sugar until fully coated - Poke a hole in the top of each donut - Pipe in Nutella filling until slightly heavy - Serve & enjoy!  • • • #Recipe #donuts #baking #bakingrecipe

How to order coffee in Greece like a pro ☕🇬🇷 Recorded at @Pandrossos_Hotel_Paros 😍*invited  Greece’s coffee culture is on another level, with some iconic coffees that locals drink every single day. Of course, Greece also has cappuccinos, lattes, americanos, flat whites and all the other coffees you’re used to. But if you’re coming to Greece, you have to try ordering coffee the local way. Here’s exactly how it works. Step one: choose your coffee. ☕ Frappé Made with instant Nescafé and water, mixed until it becomes thick and foamy. The original Greek iced coffee. ☕ Freddo Espresso A cold espresso shaken with ice until it’s frothy and refreshing. ☕ Freddo Cappuccino A freddo espresso topped with a thick layer of cold milk foam. ☕ Ελληνικός Καφές (Ellinikós Kafés) Traditional Greek coffee made in a small briki pot. It’s served with the coffee grounds still inside the cup and is traditionally used for coffee reading. Now comes the important part. How sweet do you want it? 🖤 Σκέτο (Skéto) = no sugar 🤎 Μέτριο (Métrio) = medium sweet 🍯 Γλυκό (Glykó) = sweet You can also choose which sweetener you’d like: 🍬 Ζάχαρη (Záchari) = regular sugar 🤎 Μαύρη Ζάχαρη (Mávri Záchari) = brown sugar 💊 Ζαχαρίνη (Zacharíni) = saccharin 🌱 Στέβια (Stévia) = stevia If you want milk, you can ask for: 🥛 Γάλα (Gála) = regular milk 🌾 Γάλα Βρώμης (Gála Vrómis) = oat milk 🌰 Γάλα Αμυγδάλου (Gála Amygdálou) = almond milk 🥥 Γάλα Καρύδας (Gála Karýdas) = coconut milk 🌱 Γάλα Σόγιας (Gála Sógias) = soy milk If you’re ordering a freddo cappuccino, they’ll often ask if you want: ✨ Κανέλα (Kanéla) = cinnamon 🍫 Κακάο (Kakáo) = cacao And if you’re ordering a frappé, many places will also let you add a scoop of ice cream 🍨 One thing many tourists don’t know: Freddo espresso and freddo cappuccino are usually made with TWO shots of espresso. If you’d rather have a lighter coffee, ask for: ☕ Μονή Δόση (Moní Dósi) = single shot ☕ Ελαφρύ (Elafrý) = light My personal order? ☕ Ένα Φρέντο Καπουτσίνο Μέτριο, με Μαύρη Ζάχαρη, Κανέλα και Μονή Δόση (Ena Frénto Kapoutsíno Métrio, me Mávri Záchari, Kanéla kai Moní Dósi) A freddo cappuccino, medium sweet, with brown sugar, cinnamon and a single shot.
